ui.footnote: Annual-period IRR on the partnership waterfall (the OA specifies actual-date XIRR). Warehouse figures use XIRR on dates. Ties to the v10 and SV26 workbooks to the cent at default inputs. Differences from v10: partnership cash is floored at zero each year, pref compounding is a switch (off = v10), and v10's Exit & Disposition tab is now the Custom case, which flows through every section (in v10 it fed nothing downstream). Hold period is fixed at five years. Not legal, tax or investment advice.

Whether LTEC signed a UPA and whether the Company accepted it (irrevocable on acceptance, UPA §1.3).
T-12 P&L, rent roll with concessions, and a bridge from $161.6k to $294.5k other income.
Redstone personal cash: Exhibit B shows only the rolled acquisition fee ($382k).
Disposition and refi fee percentages; PM agreement; crystallization plans (§8.7).

deal._loan_note: debt_service_method 'fixed' uses annual_debt_service (deck, $467,935); 'interest_only' = loan_amount x loan_rate, so a different assumed rate flows through. assumption_fee_pct of loan_amount is paid from Year-1 cash. Terms are open diligence item #1.
deal._hold_refi_note: hold_years: sale at the end of this year (3-10; 5 = v10/deck). Past Year 5 each line grows at the case's long-run rate; the Sponsor case sells at its deck-implied cap. refi: at the end of `year` (< hold_years) the loan is replaced: appraised value = next year's NOI / appraisal_cap (0 = the case's exit cap); loan = ltv x value or a set amount, capped so next year's debt service is covered dscr_min times (0 = no cap); interest-only for io_years, then level payments over amort_years; cost_pct of the new loan. Net proceeds (new loan - old balance - costs) go through the 8.1 order (OA 8.2); the new balance is paid off at the sale. Memo: Redstone expects to evaluate a refinance in 2031 when the current mortgage matures. crystallize: Redstone elects OA 8.7 after the refinance (fixed percentages from a hypothetical distribution of appraised value - new loan - 2% costs). side_letter_protects: LTEC's units stay on the regular waterfall unless LTEC has its unreturned capital and accrued pref back by then (LTEC side letter).

timing._note: mode 'annual' = v10/SV26 workbook convention (one distribution per year on the close anniversary); every tie-out uses it. 'schedule' = Redstone's timing (OA 8.1 quarterly, siena_frequency 4; deck: first distribution Apr 20 2027, sale Oct 2031) plus the Nov 3 2026 LTEC SV26 memo for the vehicle: semiannual member distributions mid-Feb and mid-Aug (vehicle_frequency 2, vehicle_first_distribution Aug 15 2027); LTEC retains roughly at least 50% of the most recent distribution as a cash reserve (vehicle_holdback 0.5 = keep half as much as is paid out, all released at the final distribution); acquisition fee payable after the initial SV26 distribution (acq_fee_after_first); final distribution no later than six months after Redstone's final distribution (vehicle_final_lag_months, 0-6). In schedule mode the vehicle carries any shortfall forward rather than calling capital. Each year's Siena cash is split evenly across its installments; IRRs use actual dates.

waterfall._source: OA §8.1: 6% cumulative pref -> return of capital -> 80/20 to 12% LP IRR -> 70/30 to 14% -> 60/40
waterfall._pref_compounds_note: false = v10 behavior (unpaid pref carried forward without earning pref). OA says compounded annually; flip to true to test.

warehouse._about: Vehicle warehouse & sell-down (SV26 v1 workbook, Nov 4, generalized). The vehicle invests investor.check in Siena; its Siena distributions are each case's LP distributions scaled to investor.check. Names are labels only.
warehouse._manager_reserve_note: Cash the manager keeps outside the vehicle (e.g. LTEC holds the $50k reserve itself). Funded by the manager's owners at close in proportion to manager_share, returned to the owners at that time in Year 5, and part of the cost basis in manager buy-ins. Not invested in Siena.
warehouse._admin_note: ASSUMPTION - not from any document. admin_cost_method 'fixed' uses admin_cost_per_year ($); 'pct_raise' uses admin_cost_pct x capital raised, so it scales with the raise ($15k on $1.05M = 1.43%).
warehouse._fees_note: acq_fee_pct of investor.check in Year 1; mgmt_fee_pct of capital raised, every year; both paid to the manager before the hurdle.
warehouse._people_note: amount = cash the person puts into the vehicle at close (besides their share of the manager's commitment). role: 'member' keeps units for the whole hold; 'warehouse' holds units and sells them in the sell-down; 'loan' lends to the manager at loan_rate (simple), repaid as units sell, unsold principal converting to units at par on the last sale date. Warehouse + loan amounts are the pool sales draw from. Amounts + manager_commitment should equal investor.check + reserve. manager_capital = $ the person puts into the manager at close (its capital = manager_commitment + manager_reserve; their share of it gets the manager's unit distributions, loan book and reserve). manager_share = their share of the manager's fees & promote (can differ from their capital share). Each should total the manager's capital / 100%.

selldown._note: pricing: carry_simple = par x (1 + rate x years); carry_compound = par x (1 + rate)^years; premium = par x (1 + rate), negative for a discount. credit_distributions subtracts per-unit distributions paid before the sale. buyer: a person's name (their purchase is added to their results) or any other name (an outside buyer group).

warehouse._hurdle_note: Defaults follow the Nov 3 memo: members 'in aggregate' get capital plus a 10% per annum IRR (hurdle_basis 'pooled', hurdle_type 'compound'), then 40/60 with no catch-up; promote applies to all units including LTEC's. 'per_member' gives each block of units its own hurdle from its purchase price and date; 'simple' accrues 10% simple interest on unreturned capital; promote_on_manager_units false exempts LTEC's own units.
warehouse._promote_note: promote applies to all units; warehouse_promote replaces it on pool units not yet sold.
warehouse._manager_transfers_note: Buy-ins to the manager after close: {date, buyer, seller, interest: 'both'|'capital'|'promote', mode: 'share'|'amount', share, amount, price, pricing, rate, credit_distributions}. 'both' buys the same % of capital and of fees & promote; 'capital' or 'both' are priced from cost (manager_commitment + manager_reserve) grown at rate (carry_simple / carry_compound) or x (1 + rate) (premium), less cash already paid on that interest if credit_distributions; 'amount' buys as much as that $ covers. 'promote' (fees & promote only) is bought for a set price ($, 0 = granted) for share. The buyer pays the seller directly.

_direct_investors_note: Other LPs investing in Siena directly, e.g. {"name": "Levi (direct)", "check": 250000}. Same Preferred terms as everyone, so their cash scales with the check.
